body.statement: Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 states that, when \(C_V=\{P(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\), \(F\)-identifiability of the causal effect of \(X\) on \(Y\) is equivalent to identifiability after iteratively treating as observed each functional variable whose parents have already been treated as observed.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 18. Let ⟨G, V, C_V, W⟩ be an F-identifiability tuple where C_V = {Pr(X) > 0, X ∈ X}. A causal effect of X on Y is F-identifiable wrt ⟨G, V, C_V, W⟩ iff it is identifiable wrt ⟨G, C_V, V′⟩ where V′ is obtained as follows. Initially, V′ = V. Repeat until V′ stops changing: add to V′ a functional variable from W if its parents are in V′.
